title: Agentic Sites: Building Hyper Personalized Websites — Carlos Sanchez, Adobe
talk_summary: Adobe's Carlos Sanchez demos 'agentic sites' where LLM-generated page blocks are personalized per user intent, grounded in a RAG index of the existing site and served at the edge. The transferable engineering content is narrow: continuous Promptfoo-based model/provider evaluation scoring both accuracy and latency, and the observation that small/fast models suffice for constrained generation tasks.

takeaways.technique: Continuous per-workload model/provider eval with Promptfoo
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep a fixed prompt suite per site and continuously run it across many models and OpenAI-compatible providers, scoring accuracy and latency, then pick the model per workload rather than globally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a bunch of prompts, and we look uh, we run it across a huge variety of uh, models and providers, and then we look at the accuracy, we look at the speed
takeaways.numbers: 15 prompts per example site; best config 1.1s avg latency vs 4.6s for next option

takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly optimize for speed alongside accuracy because the task has a hard latency budget, and accept 'good enough' models when they are much faster.

takeaways.technique: Right-size the model to the task's information need
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the generation task is structurally simple (choose and order blocks, write short text) so a small model suffices; no need for a frontier model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need a huge LLM to do this sort of work because you are generating text, you are deciding where to put blocks

takeaways.technique: Ground generation in a site-wide index instead of free generation
takeaways.what_they_do: They build a RAG index over the whole site and constrain the LLM to recombine existing blocks, explicitly to avoid hallucination and brand drift.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We built a rack from the whole site. So what is generated is grounded on on the existing site.

takeaways.technique: Pre-generate speculative work off the critical path
takeaways.what_they_do: They note the 'for you' recommendation page can be generated ahead of time as signals accumulate, so it doesn't need low latency when finally shown.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this you could pre-generate, right? As the user browses your site, you gather these signals, and you could keep generating
